title: Decide what Cancel does on an established-but-stalled SMB session (about 60 s wait)
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: C2 A person's decision between (a) abandoning the scan thread and (b) keeping the wait and saying so in the Stopping state: missing
C3 A design pass for the chosen option, before any build: missing
C4 Option (a) implemented: the scan thread is abandoned so Cancel frees the app before the client timeout: missing
C5 Option (b) implemented: the Stopping state says a wait of about 60 s is possible: partial

Does the person accept option (b), including that 'closing the window quits at once' rests on the loopback rig until SC-033 measures real disconnects? This is C2. Every review finding on this slice was model-disposed, and the record shows no acceptance by the person. If the person chooses (a), the design needs a new pass with a retention measurement and a late-write guard in the Scan Engine.

Does the merge wait for StalledShareTests (Network=SMB-LOOPBACK) to be run by the person on the extracted rig, or is the slice accepted with it compiled but never exercised? Recommendation: run it. It is one command of about 70 s, and the rewrite removed 311 lines.

Whether RigLock should be Local\ (kept) or Global\. Global\ would serialise concurrent runs across sign-in sessions, but the sweep still could not see another session's leftover, and it changes behaviour on a file the person's pass covers.

Whether the scaffolding is proportionate. The product change is about three small files, while the rig, hook, StallRig, four network cases, 29 tests and rules make up most of a +2242 -355 diff. Reflect's lesson is to size by the rig and by who can run it, not by the UI change.
Where the wording lives: in the App project, linked into Core.Tests as a source file, against a home in Core.
Whether the abandon rule is a name-based tripwire (scan\w*.WaitAsync) rather than something structural. It can miss a task named otherwise, and review remains the backstop.
Naming the network window cases N-001 to N-004, and the choice to end the hook's 250 ms stopping timer at scan return rather than at window close.

Nothing in the obligations was left undone. What remains is person-run by contract. StalledShareTests (C-024) has never run on the extracted rig. N-001..N-004 (C-016, C-019, C-023) passed at eafb1c3 in the person's run and were not re-run.

A person runs StalledShareTests (`eng/dotnet.ps1 test tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.csproj --filter Network=SMB-LOOPBACK`, about 70 s) at the new HEAD. It has never run since the rig moved to Rig/SmbRig.cs, and the network-check record is incomplete without it.
Fold HookCases.ps1's H-001 and H-002 into WindowCases.ps1 the next time WindowCases.ps1 has to change anyway, since that change makes the network pass stale regardless.

WindowCases.ps1's Get-RigMappings matches rig mappings case-insensitively (-match), while LoopbackShare.IsRigMapping has a case-sensitive 'fsa' prefix. It only reads mappings, so nothing is deleted wrongly, but align it to -cmatch when WindowCases.ps1 is next changed.
